questions.question:
글:
The word hamburger originally comes from Hamburg, Germany's second-largest city. Hamburger means "people or things from Hamburg" in German.
The origin of the first hamburger is not clear. However, <u>People believe that the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904.</u> A cook placed a Hamburg-style steak between two slices of bread, and people started to call such food a hamburger.

위 글의 밑줄 친 문장을 가주어 it을 이용하여 다음과 같이 바꾸어 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 네 단어로 쓰시오.

→ ___________ ___________ ___________ ___________ the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904.
questions.explanation: 원문 'People believe that the hamburger was invented in...'를 가주어 it을 사용하여 'It is believed that...'로 바꿈. '사람들은 ...라고 믿는다'는 '...라고 믿어진다'로 수동태 표현으로 변환.

The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which (A)[was written / has been written] in 1920 ⓐ________ a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines that look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

It is interesting that the idea of (B)[use / using] the word robot didn't come from Karel Čapek himself. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, which means "slave workers" ⓑ________ Czech. Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided (C)[using / to use] the word roboti. In 1938, the play was made ⓒ________ a science fiction show ⓓ________ television in Britain.

ⓐ by (수동태에서 ~에 의해)
ⓑ in (Czech라는 언어로)
ⓒ into (만들어지다로 변환)
ⓓ on (텔레비전 on television)

The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which (A)[was written / has been written] in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines that look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

It is interesting (B)[which / that] the idea of using the word robot didn't come from Karel Čapek himself. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, (C)[who / which] means "slave workers" in Czech. Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.
questions.explanation:
(A) was written: 1920년 과거 일회성 사건이므로 단순과거 수동태
(B) using: "It is interesting that..." 구문은 it이 가주어, that 절이 진주어. "the idea of using"에서 using은 동명사.
(C) to use: decided 다음에는 to부정사. "decided to use the word roboti"

위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것은?

The word hurricane comes from the Spanish word huracán, ⓐwhich originate from the name of a Mayan god. In the Mayan creation myth, Huracán is the weather god of wind, storm, and fire, and (A)he is ⓑone of the three gods whom created humans. However, the first humans angered (B)the gods, so Huracán caused a great flood.

The first Spanish contact with the Mayan civilization was in 1517. ⓒSpanish explorers who were passing through the Caribbean experiencing a hurricane and picked up the word for (C)it from (D)the people in the area. In English, ⓓone of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608.

The word hamburger originally comes from Hamburg, Germany's second-largest city. Hamburger means "people or things from Hamburg" in German.

The origin of the first hamburger is not clear. However, ⓔit is believed that the hamburger invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904. A cook placed a Hamburg-style steak between two slices of bread, and people started to call (E)such food a hamburger.
questions.explanation:
ⓐ originate → originates (which는 단수, huracán을 선행사로 함)
ⓑ whom → who (부사절에서 주어 위치, "gods who created humans")
ⓒ experiencing → experienced (과거와의 병렬, "passing through ~~ and picked up")
ⓓ was → 올바름 (one of the early uses가 주어, 단수)
ⓔ invented → was invented (it is believed that ~ 구문에서 주어는 the hamburger, 수동태 필요)

questions.question:
위 글의 밑줄 친 두 문장을 계속적 용법의 관계대명사를 이용하여 한 문장으로 바꾸어 쓰시오.

The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo. It means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage. British traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage and introduced it to Britain in the 18th century.

The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after it first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

※ 완전한 문장으로 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: 두 문장 'The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo'와 'It means "to press."'를 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which로 연결. It을 which로 바꾸고 두 문장을 한 문장으로 통합.

(B) In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

(C) The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word champo, which means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage.

________________________________________________________ Here are some examples with interesting stories.

shampoo

The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, which means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage. British traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage and introduced it to Britain in the 18th century.

The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after it first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

hamburger

The word hamburger originally comes from Hamburg, Germany's second-largest city. Hamburger means "people or things from Hamburg" in German.

The origin of the first hamburger is not clear. However, it is believed that the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904. A cook placed a Hamburg-style steak between two slices of bread, and people started to call such food a hamburger.

The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which was written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. (A) In the play, robots are machines ⓐ_________ look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory. (B)

(D) Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. (E) In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.

위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

① 정확함. "which was written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek" ← 같은 내용

스페인 탐험가들은 카리브해 지역 사람들로부터 '홍수'라는 단어를 접하게 되었다.
questions.question:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

The word hurricane comes from the Spanish word huracán, which originates from the name of a Mayan god. In the Mayan creation myth, Huracán is the weather god of wind, storm, and fire, and he is one of the three gods who created humans. However, the first humans angered the gods, so Huracán caused a great flood.

The first Spanish contact with the Mayan civilization was in 1517. Spanish explorers who were passing through the Caribbean experienced a hurricane and picked up the word for it from the people in the area. In English, one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608.
questions.explanation:
① 바람, 천둥, 불이 아니라 바람, 폭풍, 불 (storm ≠ 천둥) → 오답
② "one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare" (Hurricane 제목의 희곡 아님) → 오답
③ 1517년 = 16세기 → 정답
④ "the first humans angered the gods, so Huracán caused a great flood" (폭풍이 아니라 홍수) → 오답
⑤ "picked up the word for it" = hurricane을 나타내는 단어 (홍수 아님) → 오답
